Return exactly two columns only: compound_chembl_id and canonical_smiles.

Retrieve compounds selective for target CHEMBL2971 (Tyrosine-protein kinase JAK2) over target CHEMBL2835 (Tyrosine-protein kinase JAK1). Define selectivity exactly as: IC50 < 50 nM against CHEMBL2971 and IC50 > 200 nM against CHEMBL2835, using only rows with standard_relation = '=' and standard_units = 'nM'. Return each qualifying compound once only, using set semantics over compound identity rather than multiplicative joins between raw activity rows; intersect the JAK2 hit set and the JAK1 hit set, or deduplicate each target-specific hit set before joining. Return exactly two columns only: compound_chembl_id and canonical_smiles. The compound_chembl_id column must be the public ChEMBL compound identifier from molecule_dictionary.chembl_id, not the internal molregno numeric key.

Retrieve distinct molecule ChEMBL IDs and canonical SMILES for compounds tested in Homo sapiens assays against target CHEMBL284 (Dipeptidyl peptidase 4). Filter on assays.assay_organism = 'Homo sapiens' and return only the distinct molecule_chembl_id and canonical_smiles columns.

Retrieve IC50 activities in nM against target CHEMBL284 (Dipeptidyl peptidase 4) together with canonical SMILES, compound ChEMBL ID, compound key, PubMed ID or DOI, assay description, standard_type, standard_relation, standard_value, standard_units, activity_comment, target ChEMBL ID, target name, and target organism. For pubmed_id_or_doi, prefer the PubMed ID when both pubmed_id and doi are present; otherwise use the DOI. Join docs from activities.doc_id = docs.doc_id, and left join compound_records from activities.record_id = compound_records.record_id only to obtain compound_key. The final SELECT must be DISTINCT across exactly compound_chembl_id, canonical_smiles, compound_key, pubmed_id_or_doi, assay_description, standard_type, standard_relation, standard_value, standard_units, activity_comment, target_chembl_id, target_name, and target_organism; do not emit duplicate projected rows from many-to-many joins.
